newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee futures called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee futures called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open little changed on Monday, although some traders expected prices to head higher following Friday's finish which was well off session lows.
"Sentiment is bullish because of the way the market rallied back Friday," said one trader.

Friday, New York arabica futures recovered from an early sell-off to end mixed in light trading. September fell 2.95 cents, to 205.85 cents, after ranging between 206.50 and 201.00 cents. December rose 1.60 cents on the day, to 177.85 cents, while the back months closed 0.75 to 2.00 cents higher.
The September/December switch narrowed to 28.00 cents compared with 32.55 cents at the close on Thursday. December/March 1998 widened to 22.10 cents versus 21.25 cents the previous session.
Technically, traders said September faced resistance at 210.00 cents. Support was seen at 201.00-200.00 cents.

On the weather front, U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Monday that cooler weather is forecast this week in Brazil's coffee belt, however, no damaging cold weather is expected. Low temperatures will range from the mid-40s to mid-50s F (7-13 C).
After Friday's close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks rose by 3,190 60-kg bags as of August 7, to 94,119 bags. No coffee was pending grading, the exchange said.
London robusta futures were higher early Monday in quiet trading. At the midday break, September was up $19, at the day's high of $1,634. November rose $13, to $1,628.
